minutes.headline: Committee voted to open three school choice slots each in grades five and seven, for students already enrolled who are moving away.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered encumbering FY15 invoices, the superintendent's report on a power shutdown and transition work, and a school choice recommendation limited to current students whose families are moving. The committee also reviewed draft superintendent goals, accepted a donation for technology, and heard about playground fundraising. The next meeting is a workshop on August 13.

Members asked whether added choice students cost extra money. Staff said a little, and the choice formula requires the sending district to pay.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to open three school choice slots each in grades five and seven, for enrolled students whose families are moving out of town.
The business office presented FY15 encumbrances so funds stay available for invoices not yet received for goods and services delivered by June 30.
Staff said added choice students cost a little, and under the choice formula the sending district pays; enrollment was also down, with a revenue loss as heard.
The committee accepted a donation for middle school technology and heard that the Lions Club is raising money for the grade 3-5 playground.
Draft superintendent goals were reviewed, including FY17 budget funds for the first of three years of instructional materials.

why_it_matters: Choice slots and charter departures change enrollment, which moves the tuition revenue the school budget counts on and so affects how much falls to the town budget, mostly taxes.
Encumbering FY15 invoices keeps those bills in the year they were incurred, and the draft goal points to a multi-year curriculum materials cost that will come up in the FY17 budget.
watch_next: Workshop on August 13, to be posted as a regular meeting in case business arises.
A community service learning presentation, to be scheduled at the first April meeting.
